fix(build): a later BSR's multi-texture modifier joins the resource closure

## Summary

With `SRO_SKYTEMPLE` on, the client asset build fails in `npcModels`:

```
[npc] required model coverage incomplete; valid manifests were not replaced:
MOB_SKYTEMPLE_B_AR_FIRESPIRIT: ENOENT ... extracted\Data_extracted\prim\mtrl\etc\flame_spirit_t.ddj;
MOB_SKYTEMPLE_D_AR_FIRESPIRIT_DEMON: ENOENT ... prim\mtrl\etc\flame_spirit_t.ddj
```

**Cause.** The later-source importers (Sky Temple, Arabia, cap-110 equipment) copy each resource and everything it names through `scripts/analysis/cap110_asset_dependencies.mjs`. For a `.bsr`, that audit followed meshes, materials, skeleton, animations, sounds and particles, but **not the multi-texture modifiers** (`ModDataMultiTex` / `ModDataMultiTexRev`, already parsed by `bsrModifiers.mjs`). These name an extra texture straight from the BSR, outside every material set. `res/mob/arabia/firespirit.bsr` and `firespirit_demon.bsr` (and `flame_spirit.bsr`) name `prim\mtrl\etc\flame_spirit_t.ddj` that way. The file is in the v1.696 Data.pk2, but the importer never copied it.

**Fix.** A later resource's `multiTextureModifiers[].texturePath` joins its dependencies. A native resource's texture is native, so the closure leaves it alone, the same posture it already takes for native sound and particle owners.

## What this sends

- `scripts/analysis/cap110_asset_dependencies.mjs`: follows the multi-texture paths of non-native BSRs.
- `scripts/test/assets/assetDependencyMultiTexture.test.mjs` (registered in `scripts/test/suites/assets.mjs`): a synthetic BSR with one reversed multi-texture modifier. The texture is listed for a later resource and left out for a native one.

## Config / what to do

Nothing to configure. A variant already built with Sky Temple (or Arabia, if it places a flame spirit) gets the texture on its next import run (stage 2, or the layer's import), followed by the asset build.

## Player note

None (Sky Temple is off by default; this repairs its build).

## Old tab

Not affected (build tooling only).

## Evidence

- [x] rg: blast radius: `cap110_asset_dependencies.mjs` is spawned by `cap110_item_import.resource_dependencies` (`copy_asset_closure`, `copy_resource_closure`), used by the equipment, Sky Temple, Arabia and later-world imports; `multiTextureModifiers` producers and consumers (`bsrModifiers.mjs`, `characterMultiTexture.mjs`, `entityMaterialMetadata.mjs`) are unchanged
- [x] callers: the existing audit test (`scripts/test/world/worldLayers.test.mjs`) still passes
- [x] edge cases: native resource (left alone, tested), BSR without the modifier (unchanged path), the real v1.696 `firespirit.bsr` (checked below)
- [ ] native client: n/a - build tooling, no native claim
- [ ] native server: n/a - build tooling, no native claim
- [x] subs: n/a

## Native claims

none

## Verification

- `node --test scripts/test/assets/assetDependencyMultiTexture.test.mjs scripts/test/world/worldLayers.test.mjs`: 5/5 pass. The new test fails without the fix (checked by reverting the parser change).
- The real v1.696 `res/mob/arabia/firespirit.bsr` through the audit (`native: false`, as the Sky Temple import sends it) now lists `prim\mtrl\etc\flame_spirit_t.ddj`.
- Locally, with the texture in place, the Sky Temple variant's asset build gets past `npcModels`.
- `pnpm task check:format`: no new unformatted file; `pnpm task check:scripts`: exit 0.

Found while testing #3861 (Sky Temple on the Jangan gate) locally.

fix(build): the quick party slot's portrait disc is published (a black disc since #3699)

## Summary

Since #3699, every **quick party slot** (the party members under the player's HP bar) shows a **black disc** instead of the member's portrait, locally and on the live shard. The party window's portraits and the player's own portrait still draw.

**Cause.** #3699 draws each quick party portrait through its `CIFStaticWithPictureClip` disc as a mask: `interface/quickparty/qpt_face` (+0x380, set by 5BA64B). The build never published `qpt_face`: the runtime image catalog (`cifRuntimeImageCatalog.mjs`) lists only the slot's distance shades `qpt_face_faraway_60..100`. The UI device skips a quad whose mask texture is not loaded (`device/ui.ts`: `if ( !slot || !mask )`), so the portrait quad never draws and only the slot's black backing shows. `pt_face` (party window) and `pmi_face` / `pmi_pet_face` (player, pet) were already published, which is why only the quick party slots broke.

Checked on a built tree: `Media_extracted/interface/quickparty/` holds `qpt_face_faraway_*.png` but no `qpt_face.png`, while the native `qpt_face.ddj` exists in the v1.150 Media.

**Fix.** Publish `interface/quickparty/qpt_face.ddj` with the other quick party runtime images. A source test (`pictureClipDiscs.test.mjs`) pins every disc the client masks a portrait with (`pmi_face`, `pmi_pet_face`, `qpt_face`, `pt_face`).

## Config / what to do

Nothing to configure. The next asset build publishes the image; players get it with the release's assets.

## Player note

Player-note: UI: The party members' portraits under your HP bar show the characters again instead of a black circle.

## Old tab

Not affected (published asset only; an old tab gets the image once the assets update).

## Evidence

- [x] rg: blast radius: `runtimeCifImageReferences` (consumed by `families/looseFamilies.mjs`, `shared/cifResources.mjs`); the client's mask users in `ui.ts` (`PICTURE_CLIP_PLAYER`, `PICTURE_CLIP_PET`, `PICTURE_CLIP_QUICK_PARTY`, `popupArt.portrait`)
- [x] callers: the existing catalog tests are unchanged
- [x] edge cases: each mask disc is pinned; the distance shades are still listed
- [x] native client: the disc and its setter are cited from #3699's own reading (5BA64B sets +0x380 to qpt_face; 538600 takes alpha from stage 1)
- [ ] native server: n/a - client asset only
- [x] subs: n/a

## Native claims

| Claim | Native evidence | Checked by | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The quick party slot's picture clip disc is `interface/quickparty/qpt_face` | CIFQuickPartySlot OnCreate 5BA64B (cited in #3699's `ui.ts` comment) | reused from #3699, not re-traced | reused |

## Verification

- `node --test scripts/test/assets/pictureClipDiscs.test.mjs`: pass; it fails without the catalog line ("the build does not publish interface/quickparty/qpt_face.ddj").
- `pnpm task check:format`: no new unformatted file.
- Local asset rebuild and in-game check: in progress, I will report it here.

fix(remoting): match IPv6 coordinators by XID

- [x] I have registered the PR [changes](https://github.com/apache/incubator-seata-go/tree/master/changes) in `changes/dev.md`.

**What this PR does**

For example, a Go checkout service connected to two Seata coordinators might receive an XID with `2001:0db8:0:0:0:0:0:1` while the matching connection uses `[2001:db8::1]:8000`. The string comparison misses the match and can route the request to the other coordinator.

`XidLoadBalance` now compares the parsed IP address and port so it selects the matching connection.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**

No linked issue.

**Special notes for your reviewer**

The regression test reproduced the fallback before the fix and passed 20 runs afterward.

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**

```release-note
Fix XID routing when the XID and coordinator connection use different forms of the same IPv6 address.
```

fix(kafka): after a broker loses messages, consume a partition again from its oldest message

## The problem we're solving

`pkg/kafka` promises that every message is handled at least once, never skipped. There's one case where franz-go's default could break that.

If a broker loses messages it had already accepted (say it fails and comes back without its latest writes), a consumer's saved position may no longer exist, and it can't tell exactly where to carry on. franz-go's default then resumes at the first message stamped one minute before the last one it read. If what survived on the broker differs from what we read further back than that minute, those messages are never handled.

This barely applies today: with one broker and no copies of its data, losing data means losing the disk, and then everything is gone whatever we set. It matters once Kafka runs with replicas.

## Ways we could have solved it

- **Keep franz-go's default (go back a minute):** few duplicates, but it can skip messages.
- **Go back further, say an hour:** fewer skips than a minute, but still a guess.
- **Start the partition again from its oldest message (chosen):** never skips anything still in the topic. The cost is re-reading up to the topic's retention after such a failure, and handlers must cope with duplicates anyway. This is Kafka's `auto.offset.reset=earliest`.

## How we solved it & why we chose this

One option on `Consume`'s client in `pkg/kafka/kafka.go`: `kgo.ConsumeResetOffset(kgo.NewOffset().AtStart())`, with a comment explaining the case it covers.

It doesn't change the common cases. A new group, or a saved position older than the oldest message still in the topic (a consumer stopped for longer than the topic keeps messages), already starts at the oldest message.

## Impact on customers/users

Nothing changes for customers: no service consumes yet. For the services that will, a broker losing data means re-reading rather than skipping.

Security: none.

## How to review

| Commit | What | Read closely |
|---|---|---|
| `fix(kafka): after a broker loses messages, consume a partition again from its oldest message` | One client option, and the comment explaining it | Whether the comment matches franz-go's docs for `ConsumeResetOffset` |

## How to check it works

```bash
make check
```

There's no new test: kfake, the in-memory Kafka, can't fake a broker losing data, so any test would be fragile. The existing `pkg/kafka` tests all pass with the option set.

## Checklist

- [ ] Tests added or updated for new code (none: kfake can't fake broker data loss)
- [x] Docs added or updated (README, `docs/`, ADR if a decision was made)
- [x] `docs/security.md` still matches: its controls, known gaps and the files they link to
- [x] `AGENTS.md` updated if layout, commands or conventions changed (no change needed)
- [x] Branch name follows Conventional Branch (`feature/…`, `fix/…`, `chore/…`)
- [x] Keeps it simple: no duplication across services (DRY), no cleverness (KISS), nothing built "just in case" (YAGNI)

--- a/pkg/kafka/kafka.go
+++ b/pkg/kafka/kafka.go
@@ -158,6 +158,14 @@ func Consume(ctx context.Context, brokers []string, group string, topics []strin
 		kgo.ConsumerGroup(group),
 		kgo.ConsumeTopics(topics...),
 		kgo.DisableAutoCommit(), // workers commit what they've handled
+		// If a broker loses messages it had accepted, a member can't tell
+		// exactly where to resume. franz-go's default goes back a minute
+		// before the last message it read, which could skip one that
+		// survived; we start the partition again from its oldest message.

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(macos): hide indicators for programmatic scrolls

## Summary

- On macOS the overlay scroll indicator shows only while the user moves the view, as AppKit's overlay scrollers do: the wheel, the trackpad and the system's momentum, the indicator dragged, a pinch, a selection dragged past the edge, and the snap or spring back after a release or a pinch.
- The app's scrolls (`ScrollTo`, `ScrollToEnd`, `ScrollBy`, a focused field revealed, a refresh's room, content that shrank) move the view and leave the indicator as it is.
- The pointer over the view still shows it, as before.
- `docs/architecture/scrolling.md` describes the rule.

Closes #343

## Verification

- `go build ./...`, and builds for windows, linux, android/arm64 and js/wasm
- `go tool nsgo check -target all`
- `go tool nsgo test -run 'Layer|Skills|Doc' .`
- `go vet` and `go tool nsgo test ./internal/platform/macos` on macOS. `TestTheIndicatorShowsOnlyForTheUsersScrolls` drives a real scroll view through `scrollTo` (still and animated), `scrollBy`, a mouse wheel and a trackpad spring back. It fails if moves always show the indicator, and it fails if a spring back is treated as the app's scroll.
- `go tool nsgo test -target macos` probe on a Mac: a 300×300 scroll view over white rows, counting indicator pixels at the right edge. On main: `ScrollToEnd` gives 864 and an animated `ScrollTo` gives 860. With this PR both give 0. A platform trackpad scroll gives 862 on both.

issue #1933: 05-runs P3-06 scopes its row filter to session rows

Closes #1933.

The filter `hasText: '#1'` matched both the session row and the run row nested inside it when both had id 1. That happens when 05-runs goes first in a fresh test world. The locator now takes direct session rows with exact id text.

**Verification:** `make web-e2e E2E_ARGS='05-runs.spec.ts --repeat-each=10'` from a fresh world passed 30 of 30. `tsc` and `eslint` are clean.

**Review:** principal diff review (three lines).

issue #1931: the compact-stage rule no longer nests :has()

Closes #1931.

- `.centre:has(> .stage:not(:empty):has(.compact))` nested `:has()`, which the spec forbids, so every engine dropped the rule. It becomes `.centre:has(> .stage:not(:empty) .compact)`.
- **New check:** `web/src/app-css.test.ts` reads `app.css` and fails on any `:has(` nested inside `:has(`.
- **New layout case:** `16-layout.spec.ts` checks that the rule applies.
- Both new checks failed with the old selector and pass with the fix.

**Verification (codex, sandboxed):**
- `vitest`: 5,703 passed.
- `tsc` and `eslint`: clean.
- `make web-e2e` on `16-layout`: 9 passed.

**Review:** principal diff review. It's a one-selector fix, and one review per PR.
